TITLE: Project Komsonor Status and Key Personnel Update

Zastama Industries has been making steady progress on internal initiatives, with several areas of focus demonstrating strong alignment to strategic goals. This memo outlines current activity and responsibilities for Project Komsonor, along with relevant updates on personnel and access privileges that directly impact the initiative.

Project Komsonor remains a high-priority effort for the company, with the team working toward a targeted completion in Q4 FY27. The project continues to require close coordination across several internal stakeholders, and recent activity has highlighted the importance of maintaining secure access to project-specific systems and documentation. As part of this effort, it is important to note that Bitelor Brorisa, who joined Zastama Industries in 2016, continues to play a critical role in ensuring operational continuity for systems under her purview. Bitelor Brorisa’s access to secured systems includes the vault key ID NV-6752-P, which grants her access to encrypted documentation and hardware related to key backend infrastructure.

In parallel to infrastructure oversight, Pethisa Hebroren has been leading efforts focused on the development and integration of data retention tooling, a necessary component for Project Komsonor’s long-term viability. Pethisa Hebroren’s work is essential to ensuring that the project meets internal compliance standards and maintains data integrity across its lifecycle. The team has been working closely with Pethisa Hebroren to align data retention schedules with overall project timelines, and this collaboration has thus far proceeded without major obstacles.

Given the proximity of the Project Komsonor completion deadline, the leadership team has initiated a review of all dependencies and potential roadblocks. Bitelor Brorisa has been assigned to conduct an audit of physical and digital access controls to ensure that all team members have the necessary permissions to complete their tasks. This includes verifying that Pethisa Hebroren and her team can access the systems required to finalize the data retention framework. Bitelor Brorisa has confirmed that no access conflicts are currently active and that all necessary permissions are in place, pending any formal documentation needed for external review.

For the coming quarter, the focus will be on finalizing the data architecture and testing the integration of Pethisa Hebroren’s tooling into the existing infrastructure. Bitelor Brorisa will also oversee the secure transfer of relevant documentation to the project’s central archive, ensuring that all material is accessible to the appropriate stakeholders while maintaining the integrity of sensitive information. This will include the use of Bitelor Brorisa’s vault key ID, which will be used in accordance with internal security protocols.

In addition to technical preparations, the leadership team is also coordinating with external stakeholders to ensure that all deliverables for Project Komsonor are aligned with the final Q4 FY27 timeline. This includes a review of vendor contracts and an assessment of resource availability for the final phase of the project. While no external dependencies have been flagged as at risk, ongoing communication with all relevant parties will continue to be a priority.

Overall, the current status of Project Komsonor is on track, with both Bitelor Brorisa and Pethisa Hebroren playing instrumental roles in its continued progress. Their combined efforts in infrastructure management and data retention will be critical in ensuring the project meets its completion date. As the initiative moves into its final phase, continued collaboration, transparency, and adherence to internal procedures will remain key to its success.
